I’ll be damned if … phrase

also I’ll be darned if, damned if I know, may I die if, I swear I didn’t, I’ll be darned if I ever

classical

Plaut. Mil. 3.2.21: Dī mē perdant, sī bibī (Lewis & Short s.v. enim)
Traupman 96

Dī mē perdant, sī …

may the gods destroy me if …

(vōx cōmica: Plaut.)

An oath on oneself: what follows sī is what the speaker denies.

Other words

  • Male mī sit, sī … — I’ll be darned if …

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 13.25.3: male mī sit, sī umquam quicquam tam ēnītar; Traupman 96; Traupman 300

    (vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Cic. in epistulīs)

    “May it go badly with me if …”, with the future after sī: Cicero swears to Atticus that he will never again take such pains over a piece of writing.

Examples

  • Dī mē perdant, sī ego tuī quicquam abstulī.

    May the gods destroy me if I took anything of yours.Plaut. Aul. 4.4.19 (Lewis & Short)

  • Dī mē perdant, sī sciō.

    I’ll be damned if I know.Traupman 96

  • Male mī sit, sī umquam …

    I’ll be darned if I ever …Traupman 300

  • Male mī sit, sī umquam quicquam tam ēnītar.

    I’ll be damned if I ever take such pains over anything again.Cic. Att. 13.25.3

SourcesLewis & Short: perdo

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 96, 300.
